page: The Vultr vhf-6c-24gb is an instance in the High Frequency Compute series based on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources consist of 6 shared virtual CPUs distributed over 3 physical Intel processor cores operating at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 4 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 16 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX matrix instructions are absent. Memory capacity is configured at 24.0 GB, maintaining an even 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally attached via a 448 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Empirical benchmarks locate the vhf-6c-24gb predominantly within median performance tiers. The system achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1670.29 and a multi-core score of 9438.87, aligning with middle-tier expectations. Geekbench metrics reinforce this baseline with 1612.0 in single-core and 6307.0 in multi-core processing, alongside a Passmark CPU rating of 8278.31. Task-specific tests show strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 33.56 GB/s and Geekbench text processing at 2575.0 points. Conversely, memory bandwidth drops significantly under uncached loads, recording 26.11 GB/s for large-block reads and 13.1 GB/s for writes. Database operations and static web serving throughput also register in lower percentiles, and larger language model inference tests highlight strict CPU compute boundaries on complex models.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server balances vCPU allocation, memory density, and local high-speed NVMe storage efficiently for compute jobs that do not saturate uncached memory buses. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention under continuous maximum loads, making it less suitable for high-density transactional databases or real-time physics computing. However, its balanced resource distribution and strong text and compression metrics make it well matched for standard web application backends, CI/CD worker nodes, microservices, batch processing, and caching layers like Redis.
description: The Vultr vhf-6c-24gb is an x86_64 server instance within the High Frequency Compute family, delivering 6 shared virtual CPUs across 3 physical Intel cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 24.0 GB of system memory and 448 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Its balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio provides 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache, AVX, and AES instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations show solid middle-tier execution across CPU and memory tests, scoring 1612.0 in Geekbench single-core, 6307.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 8278.31 in Passmark CPU testing. Text processing and gzip compression demonstrate above-average throughput, while uncached memory bandwidth and static web serving exhibit lower relative performance. With no bundled discrete GPU, the instance is cost-efficient for general-purpose application hosting, text processing, CI/CD pipelines, and microservices requiring local NVMe storage.
